01

CONVENTIONAL

The familiar favorite.

A mortgage that isn’t government-insured. We’ll review how your credit, down payment, and property affect the options.

Ask about mortgage insurance and the difference between a fixed and adjustable rate.

Talk Conventional with Erik ↗
02

FHA

A different path to home.

Government-insured financing that may fit buyers who need more flexibility. Qualifying requirements still apply.

Ask about upfront and ongoing mortgage insurance, property standards, and your total cash to close.

Talk FHA with Erik ↗
03

VA

For those who’ve served.

Financing for eligible veterans, service members, and certain surviving spouses. Let’s review eligibility and the property together.

Ask about the Certificate of Eligibility, any funding fee or exemption, and remaining closing costs.

Talk VA with Erik ↗

USDA

For eligible borrowers and properties in qualifying areas. Income and location requirements matter.

Jumbo

For financing above conforming loan limits. Documentation, reserves, and credit requirements can differ.

Refinancing

A fresh look at your current mortgage, including the costs of changing it—and the option to keep it.

All programs are subject to eligibility, underwriting, property approval, and availability. Explore Patriot’s loan options ↗

PLAIN ENGLISH INCLUDED

Good questions.
Uncomplicated answers.

Do I need to know which loan I want?

No. Tell me about your situation and we can review the options together. Loan eligibility depends on your finances, the property, and program requirements.

What should I have ready?

Start with your goals and timeline. For an application, expect requests for income and asset documentation, identification, and information about debts and the property. Your exact checklist depends on your situation. Use Patriot’s secure application for sensitive documents.

Is the lowest rate always the best deal?

Compare the rate alongside lender fees, points, mortgage insurance, monthly payment, and cash to close. Ask for comparable Loan Estimates so you can understand the tradeoffs.

Does boring mean nothing can go wrong?

No lender can promise that. Boring means aiming for a prepared, well-explained process: identifying issues early, communicating clearly, and helping you understand the next step.
